- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–5% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods of a 30-day forecast; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overreacts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3 consecutive days, model is lagging; adjust forward by +1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
